facts.text: Ladonia was originally called McCownville and changed its name in 1857, supposedly honoring A.
The arrival of the Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe Railway in 1887 turned Ladonia into an agricultural marketing hub for cotton, corn, oats, and wheat.
Ladonia Fossil Park, just 2 miles north on the North Sulphur River, attracts fossil hunters who find shark teeth and Mosasaur vertebrae.
The town’s early settlers included James McFarland, Daniel Davis, and merchant Frank McCown, who helped establish the first house and store.
The Ladonia Historical Preservation Society, now the Burleson History Center, publishes books on local history and offers scanned copies on its website.
